subject: Exec concession request: hosted API tiered-rate exception for Helium Health pilot
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@heliumhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@heliumhealth.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot commercial terms — ask for hosted API rate flexibility

Hi Marissa / Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Helium Health is excited. We have a short pilot we want to run across three hospital customers in Q3, and your hosted API is a great fit. Before we lock the SOW, procurement asked if Redwood can offer a deeper introductory rate for the first 12 months.

High level ask:
- 30% off your standard Hosted API usage rates for the initial 12-month pilot period
- Commitment: 12 months, estimated monthly usage ~120M tokens/month (see attached forecast)
- Requirement: data residency in us-east region and SOC2 attestations (we already have the SOC2 NDA addendum)

We understand this is a material concession; our justification is that this pilot is a strategic pathway to a multi-region rollout across 150+ hospital sites in 2029 if the POC meets latency and accuracy SLAs. We can agree to an 18-month ramp if Redwood needs longer-term visibility.

Attached: HeliumHealth_MonthlyForecast.xlsx (initial consumption plan)

Can you share what level of discount your sales leadership/finance would consider? If it's >20% we can loop in our CFO and sign a binding SOW quickly.

Best,
Emma
Emma Li
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Helium Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot commercial terms — ask for hosted API rate flexibility

Hi Emma — appreciate the clear numbers and the forecast.

Short answer: we can consider an introductory concession, but anything greater than 20% requires exec authorization and a tightening of commercial protections (minimum monthly commitment + signed SOW + SOC2 addendum). I've attached the draft SOW and our usage rollup so you and procurement can confirm monthly floors.

Proposed mutual action plan:
- Helium: confirm monthly minimum spend you can commit to in the SOW (we need a guaranteed floor)
- Redwood: sales to request executive concession if the ask remains above 20%
- Legal (Rafael): prepare a narrow concession addendum that automatically reverts to standard rates after 12 months unless a multi-year enterprise agreement is signed

Emma — can you confirm you can do an 18-month ramp clause or a higher minimum monthly guarantee? If yes, I will escalate internally today.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Helium Health pricing request — recommendation for exec approval

Team — quick assessment of Helium Health ask and my recommendation.

Summary:
- External asks: 30% off Hosted API for 12 months; estimated 120M tokens/mo for pilot
- Requested concession is >20% so requires executive sign-off per pricing policy
- Strategic rationale: proof-of-concept touches several marquee hospital customers and likely expands to a national roll in 2029. Competitive risk: if we decline, they may evaluate other hosted API vendors who are aggressively priced.

Commercial proposal I recommend we escalate (numbers below):
- Concession: approve 28% off list Hosted API usage rates for first 12 months
- Conditions: 18-month minimum commitment (month-to-month drawdown but with an 18-month spend guarantee) OR signed SOW with a minimum monthly spend of $70k/mo for the pilot period
- Guardrails: automatic reversion to standard pricing after 12 months unless an enterprise agreement is fully executed; legal to insert a clawback for over-consumption credits if forecast is materially wrong (>40% variance)

Why 28%? It strikes a balance: gives Helium a material signal of partnership, keeps unit economics in check if the minimum spend is met, and creates an urgency to convert to a larger enterprise contract.

Financials (back-of-envelope): if they meet the $70k/mo floor, Redwood breaks even on incremental capacity by month 6 and realizes retention upside in year 2. We can refine with finance if needed.

Request: Marissa — can you route to Rishi and Finance for final sign-off? Rafael, please prepare the concession language (short addendum) and mark the reversion and clawback language. I can join the call with Helium if they push for ~30%.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: Requesting exec authorization for 28% hosted API concession — Helium Health (DL-2028-HELIUM-042)

Rishi — short note and ask for decision.

Helium Health is requesting a 30% introductory discount on Hosted API usage for a 12-month pilot tied to an estimated 120M tokens/month. Neha asked for escalation after discussing commercial protections; Ben recommends approving a 28% concession conditioned on an 18-month minimum commit or $70k/mo guaranteed spend. Rafael will prepare a short concession addendum with automatic reversion after 12 months and a clawback for forecast variance.

Why I support exception (high level):
- Strategic pipeline: the POC targets three high-profile hospital systems that are referenceable in the US market; probability of upsell to enterprise agreement estimated at 45% within 12 months if POC meets latency/quality SLAs
- Competitive defense: competing vendors are offering deep first-year discounts; declining risks losing an entry into a cluster of hospitals
- Risk controls: commitment or minimum floor + automatic reversion + clawback reduces long-term revenue risk

Ask: please confirm one of the following by EOD Monday PST:
A) Approve the 28% concession under the conditions above (Marissa to notify customer and Rafael to push addendum)
B) Counter-offer to cap concession at 20% and require a higher minimum monthly spend ($90k/mo)
C) Deny and keep standard pricing (Neha will communicate)

Attached docs for review: HeliumHealth_MonthlyForecast.xlsx, HeliumHealth_SOW-draft.pdf, usage_rollup_2028Q2.csv
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/DL-2028-HELIUM-042

Marissa Cole
